name: AI features require segment-anything and PyTorch 2.7.1+
answer:
ANSWERED, AND ALREADY BUILT IN PHASE 2. The question had two parts.

ARE PRE-RELEASE OR NIGHTLY PYTORCH BUILDS SUPPORTED? Yes, when the version is at or above the 2.7.1 minimum - and the build is reported as a pre-release rather than silently treated as a release, so an odd failure later is explicable. There is no reason to refuse a nightly that is newer than the floor, and refusing one is not what the legacy code does either; it does something considerably worse.

DOES THE UNCAUGHT ValueError STOP THE APP FROM STARTING? Yes. `ai_availability.py` computes the version as `[int(p) for p in torch.__version__.split("+")[0].split(".")[:3]]` inside a guard that catches only ImportError. A nightly reports '2.8.0a0', so the third part is '0a0', `int()` raises ValueError, nothing catches it, and the import-time check takes the application down. The failure mode is the worst available combination: a user on a NEWER PyTorch than required cannot start LazyLabel at all, and the traceback points at a file whose entire job is to answer 'are the AI features available?'. A check for whether a feature is present should never be able to stop the program, and this one stops it for being too up to date.

THE ANSWER IS IN `modernized/lazylabel-reimagined/inference/src/lazylabel_inference/availability.py`, built as part of the Phase 2 scaffold because it needs no model and no PyTorch to be correct. The parser is total: `parse_version` returns None for anything it cannot read instead of raising, and `check_availability` turns every outcome into a reported reason - not installed, too old, unreadable, segment-anything missing, or available. An unreadable version disables the AI features and says so; it does not crash, and it does not optimistically assume the build is fine.

Tested at `inference/tests/test_availability.py` against every string the card names - 2.7.1, 2.7.1+cu124, 2.8.0a0, 2.10.0rc1, 2.7.1.dev20250101+cpu - and against unreadable input, with the version injected so none of it requires installing the build that produces it. That is the part legacy could not have tested even if it had wanted to.

One design point worth recording for Phase 3: in the web rebuild this check no longer gates a button in the same process. The inference service answers it on `/health` with the reason attached, the API relays it, and the web app disables the AI tools with that reason shown. A user who cannot use the AI tools is told why and what to install, instead of finding a dead control.
corrections: Confirmed rather than assumed the ValueError path: the card's edge case is accurate and the consequence is that a newer-than-required PyTorch prevents startup entirely.
Recorded that the availability answer now travels over /health with its reason, rather than being a local boolean, because three processes need it.
